# the contributor audit: dominated centroid and direct midpoint coupling



Sources fully read:

* `candidate 660db01ed45063dd`
* `accepted fact 486fe778f838d99d,f6641f09c19819a3`

## Dominated-centroid theorem: PASS

Normalize |K|=1. Domination gives 0<=alpha<=1 and 0<=r<=s, alpha-r<=1-s. The cap root V(t)^(1/d) is concave on the projection interval by the actual Minkowski inclusion of caps. Its projection distribution has no atoms and positive density in the interior, so V(X) is uniform. The eta pushforward is dominated by this uniform measure. Jensen at the actual centroid of K+2eta and the two disjoint interval bathtub inequalities have the displayed directions. They give phi(U)+2phi(Q)+2phi(E)>=2/(d+1), including alpha=0 and all endpoint choices. The actual centroid lies inside K, hence 0<s<1.

The Fenchel maximum of phi(t)+a t is (1+a)_+^(d+1)/(d+1), attained at t=(1+a)_+^d. The three multipliers 1/d, 1/(2d), and -L/(2d) yield precisely D=U+Q-L E. The target ratio is equivalent to D<1+4A/3. The coefficient calculation leading to Delta_d has no lost dimension factor.

The finite certificate is a rational identity: 2Z/J=2+(1+1/d)(1+A/3), B/J=1+1/(2d), N/J=1-L/(2d). Hence Delta_d=2[ZJ^d-B^(d+1)-N^(d+1)]/J^(d+1). The printed remainders provide positive integer certificates; independent agents also reconstructed all thirteen.

For d>=14, monotonicity of x log(1+1/x) and 8*15^14>21*14^14 give L>5/2. The printed exponential tail 87/32 is a valid upper bound for e. The printed positive Taylor sum bounds exp(5/4) below. The two negative terms sum to less than 31/8+33/(20d), whereas the positive terms exceed 31/8+15/(8d). The difference is positive uniformly. No asymptotic approximation is used.

Closed continuous cap boundaries carry no rho or eta mass. Pure integer normals in the mixed application must be handled separately and are handled by the full middle and one endpoint. Every containing halfspace can be moved inward to the selected point.

Pointwise strict inequalities cannot alone be passed through an infimum. The source was amended after the independent audit: writing epsilon_d=d Delta_d/(d+1)>0 gives a uniform surplus proportional to s; Jensen supplies s>=Gamma_d/3^d. This fixes strict raw-depth wording. The non-strict theorem never depended on that repair.

## Direct conditional midpoint coupling: PASS

The projection-interior identity ensures each conditional body is full dimensional. Slice-volume root concavity supplies the required interior continuity; truncated conditional volumes similarly give continuous conditional distribution functions. Their own-coordinate derivative is positive and continuous. No assertion at an excluded projection boundary is needed.

The recursive conditional quantile map is triangular and bijective between interiors. The product of own-coordinate derivatives telescopes to one because the total volumes agree. The Fubini substitution lemma is valid by iterated one-dimensional changes of variable on recursive interval domains; prefix inverse continuity and endpoint continuity ensure the image domains have the required form. Cross-coordinate differentiability is not used.

The midpoint map is injective by the first differing coordinate. Its own-coordinate product is at least one by arithmetic-geometric mean. The same Fubini substitution produces an actual midpoint density at most one after multiplying the probability law by the common volume. Compact support and both first moments are exact. All discarded body boundaries have Lebesgue measure zero.

The cap indicator implication is pointwise for closed caps, including equality. The integer offset cancels under the midpoint operation. Thus one fixed actual coupling controls every oblique ambient halfspace simultaneously, with no direction-dependent choice of coupling.

## Consequences and limitations

For A,K,B at -1,0,1 with equal endpoint volume v and K containing (A+B)/2, the point with continuous coordinate [v g_A+|K|g_K+v g_B]/(|K|+2v) is a single actual point of the middle fiber. Its raw depth is at least (3/4)Gamma_d(|K|+v). Since |K|>=v, this is at least (Gamma_d/2)(|K|+2v), proving OC for this three-fiber class in every d>=1.

The argument does not assign the mass of arbitrary many fibers to one midpoint, and does not treat unequal endpoint volumes without a further estimate. It is not a proof of arbitrary-n,d OC. The new coupling source is restricted to full-dimensional endpoint convex bodies; the separate intrinsic reductions must be invoked and checked in any broader application.
